meta.title: Who is actually arriving in New Zealand
meta.standfirst: Non-New Zealand citizen arrivals reached 209,930 in the year to October 2023, close to 3 times the pre-COVID norm. Scroll to see how old those arrivals were, where they came from, and what visas they held.
sources: Statistics NZ ITM552301 — migrant arrivals and departures by citizenship.
Statistics NZ ITM552101 — migrant arrivals and departures by age group and sex.
Statistics NZ ITM553001 — migrant arrivals by citizenship, visa type and country of last permanent residence, 12/16-month rule.
MBIE Migration Data Explorer, W3 — approved work visa decisions by nationality and occupation skill level, year ended May.
notes: Every series is a rolling 12-month sum, so each point counts the previous year.
Stats NZ does not publish the age breakdown split by citizenship, so the age chart covers all citizenships. Every other chart is non-New Zealand citizens.
Country of last permanent residence (CLPR) is where a person lived before arriving, which is a closer match for 'from India' than citizenship alone.
Figures use the 12/16-month rule and the latest months are provisional.

Skill-level figures cover approved work visas where MBIE recorded an occupation, about 60% of decisions; open work-right holders such as Working Holiday and Relationship visas are largely excluded. They run on a year-ended-May calendar, a different measure to the arrivals figures elsewhere on this page.

'Lower-skill' follows MBIE's ANZSCO skill-level scale: Level 1 is the highest, typically a bachelor's degree or higher, and Level 5 the lowest, typically no formal qualification beyond secondary school. This story counts Levels 4 and 5 combined as lower-skill.

steps.title: Two decades of migrant flows
steps.body: Arrivals of non-New Zealand citizens sit above the line, their departures below it, and the white line is the net difference between the two.

steps.title: Arrivals did all the moving
steps.body: Arrivals drive the cycles, hitting a low of 18,261 as borders closed to a peak of 209,930 in the year to October 2023.

steps.title: The same arrivals, split by age
steps.body: Stats NZ publishes the age breakdown for all citizenships together, so this chart includes returning New Zealanders. The six bands stack to total arrivals.

steps.title: People 30 and under carry the intake
steps.body: The under-20 and 20s bands together account for 54% of arrivals in the year to May 2026, 70,678 people out of 130,678. That share has not fallen below 45% at any point in two decades.

steps.title: The 30s and 40s peaked with the post-Covid surge
steps.body: Prime-working-age arrivals reached 43% of the total in the year to September 2023, up from 33% in the year to March 2019. They have since settled back to 35%.

steps.title: Three names beyond India and China
steps.body: The UK and Australia are named because they were the two largest non-NZ sources in January 2005, at 19% and 10% of arrivals. The Philippines is named too: from 1.6% back then it has grown to 10%, now bigger than the UK or Australia on their own.

steps.title: India, China and the Philippines now dominate inflows
steps.body: The three countries supplied 44,356 of 104,516 non-NZ arrivals in the year to May 2026, a combined 42%. In January 2005 they accounted for 17%.

steps.title: Zooming in on India
steps.body: These are arrivals whose last permanent residence was India, split by the visa they held. Arrivals from India peaked at 38,463, against 209,930 from other countries.

steps.title: Work visas powered the surge
steps.body: Work visa arrivals peaked at 16,404 in the year to February 2024, 43% of all India arrivals, as the Accredited Employer Work Visa replaced Essential Skills. The April 2024 reforms cut that band to 3,595 by May 2026, and shifted its skill mix too: the lower-skill share peaked at 57% in 2024 before falling back to 36% in 2026, according to MBIE data.

steps.title: The Philippines has more varied visa types
steps.body: Once the border reopened in August 2022, work and residence visas grew almost in lockstep, reaching 36% and 37% of 31,508 arrivals by October 2023. Visitor visas are now the largest band, at 33%. Work visa holders have a similar share of low-skilled visas as India: 37% in 2026.

steps.title: Students dominate China's arrivals
steps.body: Student visas make up 40% of China's arrivals (5,610 people) while work visas fell from a peak of 11,214 to 3,322. For India the student share is 32%. China's work visas stay the most skilled: its lower-skill share was just 11% in 2026, against 36% for India and 37% for the Philippines.

steps.title: Where they actually land
steps.body: Net international migration per 1,000 residents by territorial authority, over the three years ended June 2025. Rates run from -4.9 to 70.8, and 3 of 67 authorities recorded a net outflow.

steps.title: The highest rates are not the biggest places
steps.body: Queenstown-Lakes leads at 70.8 per 1,000, but that is only 3,810 people. Auckland sits 7th on the rate at 55.0 and takes 99,800, 52% of the national total.

steps.title: Auckland is not one place either
steps.body: The same measure across Auckland's local board areas. The spread inside the city, 1.2 to 102.1 per 1,000, is wider than the spread across the country as a whole.

steps.title: South and central Auckland absorb the most
steps.body: Ōtara-Papatoetoe took 10,100 people, 102 per 1,000 residents, against 1.2 in Rodney at the other end of the city.
